# casdoor_model (Resource)

Manages a Casdoor model, the Casbin model used by permissions and enforcers.

Only the attributes set in the configuration are written to Casdoor. The other fields of the object, including the ones not listed here, keep their current values.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "casdoor_model" "rbac" {
  owner        = casdoor_organization.acme.name
  name         = "rbac"
  display_name = "RBAC"
  model_text   = <<-EOT
    [request_definition]
    r = sub, obj, act

    [policy_definition]
    p = sub, obj, act

    [role_definition]
    g = _, _

    [policy_effect]
    e = some(where (p.eft == allow))

    [matchers]
    m = g(r.sub, p.sub) && r.obj == p.obj && r.act == p.act
  EOT
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the model, unique within its owner.
- `owner` (String) The organization that the object belongs to.

### Optional

- `description` (String) The description.
- `display_name` (String) The display name.
- `model_text` (String) The Casbin model, in the Casbin CONF format.

### Read-Only

- `created_time` (String) The time when the model was created.
- `id` (String) The ID of the model in the `owner/name` format.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the organization and the name.
terraform import casdoor_model.example <organization>/<name>
```
